reviews.disputed_proposition: Remove all unverified Buenos Aires City numeric propositions from the INCAA record; add Buenos Aires only as a separately researched identity.
reviews.short_rationale: INCAA does not offer a national cash rebate; Buenos Aires City operates its own BA Producción Internacional rebate via its Film Commission.
reviews.final_recommended_canonical_treatment: Keep ar_incaa_incentive non-priceable. Do not copy BAFC economics into it.

reviews.disputed_proposition: Do not aggregate three Screen NSW streams into one rate/cap record.
reviews.short_rationale: Screen NSW operates distinct streams (Production Fund, Made in NSW, etc.) which cannot be aggregated into a single formulaic rate/cap.
reviews.final_recommended_canonical_treatment: Keep out of deterministic base pricing; split stream identities before any grant modeling.

reviews.disputed_proposition: Separate VSI from the Victorian Production Fund; add the current VSI QVE thresholds.
reviews.short_rationale: VicScreen VSI is an attraction grant of up to 10%, while the Victorian Production Fund is a distinct stream. They must be modeled separately.
reviews.final_recommended_canonical_treatment: No deterministic pricing; split the two program identities.

reviews.disputed_proposition: Do not classify ANCINE as non-economic; classify the named mechanism as financing support and keep RioFilme separate.
reviews.short_rationale: ANCINE has a 70% withholding tax reduction mechanism that acts as financing support, not a non-economic program or a traditional cash rebate.
reviews.final_recommended_canonical_treatment: No deterministic QPE pricing. Preserve as financing support; create RioFilme only under a separate municipal identity.

reviews.disputed_proposition: Replace 40%+5%+5%=50% with 30% base plus applicable 5-point conditions, capped at 40%; model track-specific thresholds and uplifts.
reviews.short_rationale: The Indian incentive is a 30% base with two conditional 5% uplifts (for Indian crew and SIC), capped at 40%, not a 50% total.
reviews.final_recommended_canonical_treatment: Do not implement one 50% rule. Require project track, QPE, Indian-crew percentage, SIC status and approval.

reviews.disputed_proposition: Delete the unsupported case-by-case production-rebate claim and split ETC, bond and duty mechanisms.
reviews.short_rationale: Jamaica's ETC is a 30% credit against PAYE tax obligations for local companies, not a direct production QPE cash rebate.
reviews.final_recommended_canonical_treatment: Do not model a percentage-of-QPE incentive; preserve as financing/tax-relief support by mechanism.

reviews.disputed_proposition: Do not rename EFICINE in place. Add EFICA as a separate identity and retain EFICINE for its distinct statutory program.
reviews.short_rationale: EFICA (2026) is a new 30% transferable tax credit for international productions, distinct from the older EFICINE tax shelter.
reviews.final_recommended_canonical_treatment: Create a separate mx_efica identity; require project type, Mexico cost, supplier structure, approval and transfer assumptions.

reviews.disputed_proposition: Replace current 20%/18% brackets with 20% baseline/25% conditional uplift and apply effective-date rules.
reviews.short_rationale: As of 2026, the NZ PDV rebate is 20% base with a 5% uplift (total 25%) subject to an objective test, not the historical 20%/18% tiering.
reviews.final_recommended_canonical_treatment: Version by PDV start date; require QNZPE and uplift-test result.

reviews.disputed_proposition: Reclassify CIPA as enacted and regulated; retain an operational-readiness gate during the regulation's implementation window.
reviews.short_rationale: Peru's Law 32309 (CIPA) was enacted and regulated in June 2026 via Supreme Decree 099-2026-EF, making it an operative tax credit/certificate.
reviews.final_recommended_canonical_treatment: Model only after investor regime, approved investment, export-production status, tax-liability utilization and transfer value are known.

reviews.disputed_proposition: Use current RIPAC regulation: medium documentary/no-filming minimum EUR200k and cap EUR1.5m; distinguish large FCFS track from medium scored rounds.
reviews.short_rationale: Portugal's RIPAC under SCRI.PT (2026) is divided into two mutually exclusive tracks (Large-Scale and Medium-Budget) that must be modeled independently.
reviews.final_recommended_canonical_treatment: Split or explicitly model large and medium RIPAC tracks; price only after cultural score, track, expense geography and allocation status.

reviews.disputed_proposition: Rename/restructure away from Uruguay XXI; separate ACAU cash-rebate calls from the July 2026 tax credit; discard the unsupported generic three-tier table.
reviews.short_rationale: Uruguay XXI is just a promotional agency. ACAU administers the actual incentives, which now include both a Cash Rebate and a new 2026 Audiovisual Tax Credit.
reviews.final_recommended_canonical_treatment: Create separate ACAU program identities. Require instrument, eligible Uruguay spend, applicant/taxpayer, committee approval, current call availability and transfer assumptions.
